lastCompletedStory.title: Durable sidecar-stalled marker written on firewall-init failure and surfaced at orchestrator boot

nextStoryContext: US-001 shipped the shared .cam-sidecar-stalled.json marker module (src/supervisor/sidecar-stalled.ts: SIDECAR_STALLED_FILENAME, SidecarStalledMarker{reason,detail,writtenAt}, read/write/remove never-throw helpers) plus the firewall-init-failed producer wired into runContainerEnsureGuard (src/commands/sidecar.ts): write on FirewallError catch, remove on every healthy-boot return path (host-mode no-op AND container-mode ensure success), since the whole read+write+remove lifecycle lives inside that single boot-time-only guard function (see patterns.md 2026-07-11 bullet on this). US-002 (sidecar-died producer + liveness watcher) reuses this SAME marker file/module -- do NOT create a second marker file; just write with reason:'sidecar-died' from the new watcher. Orchestrator surfacing (boot-read item 12 + opening-blocker '⚠ sidecar stalled: <reason> — <detail>' line, read-only, not deleted by the orchestrator) is already done in templates/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md and embedded via bun run embed-vendor -- US-002 does not need to touch that doc again unless the surfaced fields change shape.
